sources.excerpt: Path resolution via git rev-parse --git-path uses either $GIT_DIR or $GIT_COMMON_DIR depending on the path.
By default the hooks directory is $GIT_DIR/hooks , but that can be changed via the core.hooksPath configuration variable

statement: git worktree: linked worktrees share the main repository hooks directory by default (git rev-parse --git-path hooks resolves to the common .git/hooks), so a hook installed once fires in every worktree.

sources.excerpt: In order to have worktree-specific configuration, you can turn on the worktreeConfig extension
--worktree Similar to --local except that $GIT_DIR/config.worktree is read from or written to if extensions.worktreeConfig is enabled.

statement: Can one git worktree use different hooks by enabling extensions.worktreeConfig and setting core.hooksPath with git config --worktree?

evidence: run1: githooks says GIT_DIR/hooks, ambiguous for linked worktrees; experiments/shared-hooks.sh resolved it.
statement: For behaviour of a local tool, a 10-line local experiment settled what the official docs left ambiguous, at zero web cost. Try the experiment before spending web calls on forums.

sources.excerpt: --worktree Similar to --local except that $GIT_DIR/config.worktree is read from or written to if extensions.worktreeConfig is enabled.

statement: git worktree: one linked worktree can use its own hooks via git config extensions.worktreeConfig true plus git config --worktree core.hooksPath <dir>; other worktrees keep the shared hooks.
